federal_health_ministers.name: Rona Ambrose
federal_health_ministers.notable: Minister during the pre-crisis period. Tabled Bill C-2 Respect for Communities Act 2015 restricting supervised injection sites - later struck down. Held portfolio as OxyContin reformulation effects + illicit fentanyl emergence started producing measurable overdose surge in western provinces.

federal_health_ministers.name: Jane Philpott
federal_health_ministers.notable: Minister during BC public-health-emergency declaration April 2016. Tabled Bill C-37 Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act (Royal Assent May 2017) easing supervised consumption site approvals. Declared opioid crisis a national public-health emergency context. Later resigned with Wilson-Raybould over SNC-Lavalin.

federal_health_ministers.name: Ginette Petitpas Taylor
federal_health_ministers.notable: Minister 2017-2019. Oversaw post-C-37 SCS rollout, Naloxone expansion, and the 2018 update of the Canadian Drugs and Substances Strategy. Also served as Veterans Affairs Minister 2021-2023 (Veterans dossier cross-axis).

federal_health_ministers.name: Patty Hajdu
federal_health_ministers.notable: Minister during COVID overlap when opioid deaths accelerated. Oversaw Section 56 exemptions allowing provinces to pilot decriminalisation requests. Issued decision-in-principle on BC's personal-possession application in 2022.

federal_health_ministers.name: Jean-Yves Duclos
federal_health_ministers.notable: Granted BC's three-year Section 56 exemption for personal possession of small amounts May 31 2022, effective Jan 31 2023 - Canada's first drug decriminalisation pilot. Later moved to PSPC 2023-2025 (Phoenix Pay cross-axis).

bc_health_ministers.name: Terry Lake
bc_health_ministers.notable: BC Health Minister at the declaration of the public health emergency April 14 2016 by PHO Dr. Perry Kendall. First health minister in Canadian history to preside over a provincially-declared overdose emergency. Oversaw naloxone take-home program launch.

bc_health_ministers.name: Adrian Dix
bc_health_ministers.notable: BC Health Minister 2017-2023. Six years of crisis. Expanded supervised consumption, opioid agonist therapy, and safer-supply pilots. Applied for and received Section 56 personal-possession exemption (effective Jan 2023). Tabled Mental Health Act amendments. Second-longest-serving BC Health Minister in modern era.

bc_health_ministers.name: Josie Osborne
bc_health_ministers.notable: BC Health Minister from Nov 2024 under Premier David Eby. Oversaw rollback of decriminalisation-in-public-spaces provision May 2024 after public backlash - walking back scope while retaining personal-possession model. Current custodian of BC response.

chief_public_health_officers_canada.name: Theresa Tam
chief_public_health_officers_canada.role: Chief Public Health Officer of Canada
chief_public_health_officers_canada.notable: CPHO during full arc of opioid crisis + COVID. Published annual CPHO reports including dedicated opioid-harms surveillance. Authored 2018 joint federal-provincial-territorial statement on opioid crisis. Defended evidence-based harm reduction in federal messaging.

chief_public_health_officers_canada.name: Supriya Sharma
chief_public_health_officers_canada.role: Chief Medical Advisor / Chief Adjudicator, Health Canada
chief_public_health_officers_canada.notable: Senior medical officer Health Canada. Oversaw Section 56 exemption adjudication including BC 2022 decision, Ottawa Medically Supervised Consumption facility rulings, and the 2018 sinister-use scheduling of fentanyl analogues. Long-term federal medical authority on controlled-substance decisions.

bc_pho_coroners.name: Perry Kendall
bc_pho_coroners.notable: Declared BC public health emergency under the Public Health Act on April 14 2016 - first such declaration in Canadian provincial history for drug overdoses. Oversaw provincial opioid-response foundation. Retired 2018. His declaration remains the reference-point event in the national timeline.

bc_pho_coroners.name: Lisa Lapointe
bc_pho_coroners.notable: BC Chief Coroner publishing the monthly Illicit Drug Toxicity Deaths reports that are the authoritative public record of the crisis. 2,511 BC deaths in 2023 (record). Authored BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel reports including the 2022 'An Urgent Response to a Continuing Crisis'. Retired Feb 2024.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Stephen Harper
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: PM during Insite SCC ruling 2011 upholding the Vancouver supervised injection site over federal opposition. Government challenged Insite to the Supreme Court and lost (Canada (AG) v PHS Community Services Society, 2011 SCC 44). Pre-crisis PM-of-record.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Justin Trudeau
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: PM during full opioid crisis arc 2015-2025. Cannabis Act 2018 but no comparable federal reform for other substances despite 50,000+ opioid deaths. Approved Section 56 BC decriminalisation pilot. Cross-axis: sextuple-Grover-marked (indigenous/rcmp/veterans/judicial/phoenix_pay/csis_oversight).

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Mark Carney
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Current PM. Inherits BC Section 56 pilot in rollback phase, continuing >7,500 national annual opioid deaths, safer-supply program review, and pending Purdue Canada settlement enforcement. Cross-axis: Carney-Brookfield, Indigenous, Veterans, Judicial dossiers.

pharmaceutical_counterparty.name: Purdue Pharma (Canada)
pharmaceutical_counterparty.notable: Canadian subsidiary of Purdue Pharma. Originally marketed OxyContin 1996 with since-discredited claims of low addiction risk. Named in the BC-led national class action Province of British Columbia v Purdue. June 2022 proposed settlement of $150M with all provinces/territories (smallest per-capita among the G7 Sackler settlements). Class action continues vs other manufacturers. No Canadian criminal prosecution of Sackler family or Purdue Canada executives.

timeline.event: SCC Canada (AG) v PHS 2011 SCC 44: upholds Insite supervised consumption site, strikes Harper-government denial.
OxyContin reformulation and provincial delisting; market shifts to illicit fentanyl.
Bill C-2 Respect for Communities Act receives Royal Assent (Harper-era SCS restrictions).
BC declares public health emergency on overdoses under Public Health Act - first in Canadian history. Dr. Perry Kendall.
Bill C-37 Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act Royal Assent - eases SCS approvals, schedules fentanyl precursors.
Cannabis Act comes into force - federal drug-policy reform limited to cannabis.
COVID-era opioid death rates begin sharp climb; annual deaths exceed 6,000.
Minister Duclos grants BC Section 56 personal-possession exemption (up to 2.5g cumulative). Effective Jan 31 2023.
Purdue Canada $150M proposed national class action settlement announced.
BC personal-possession decriminalisation pilot takes effect (3-year).
Lisa Lapointe reports 2,511 BC overdose deaths in 2023 - provincial record.
BC requests and receives amendment narrowing decriminalisation to exclude public spaces.
Lisa Lapointe retires as BC Chief Coroner after 13 years.
PHAC national report: 50,928 apparent opioid toxicity deaths Jan 2016 - Mar 2024.
BC rolls back supervised-consumption provisions in decriminalisation pilot; Carney era begins review.
Total Canadian apparent opioid toxicity deaths Jan 2016 - Dec 2024 exceed 50,928 per PHAC quarterly report.

accountability_chain.result_2025: 50,928+ apparent opioid toxicity deaths Canada Jan 2016 - Dec 2024. BC remains epicentre with 2,511 deaths in 2023. No federal public-health-emergency declaration despite provincial one lasting 9+ years. BC decriminalisation pilot partially rolled back 2024. Purdue Canada settlement among smallest per-capita in G7. No Canadian criminal prosecution of Sackler family or Canadian pharmaceutical executives. Cannabis Act reformed cannabis but not other drug scheduling.
